surfaces.part: dark purple ground tile with speckle noise and a few crack lines

answer.evidence: The image is a full 96x96 opaque tile with a uniform dark purple texture and scattered lighter speckles and thin crack lines. The silhouette is 96 wide on every row, so there is no outline, no front-edge line, no eave shadow and no ellipse. The column scans show only noise, with no band structure. It is a flat terrain tile with no standing object and no front face, so it is a top-down texture, which is expected for terrain.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a dark purple stone/soil ground with scattered lighter speckles and a few pinkish crack strokes. It measures 7 visible tones per tile, 0% near-flat coverage and 0% neutral dark edges. That matches the paving reference on tones (7) and beats the grass reference (3). Against that, it uses only 9 distinct colours in total, versus 80 for the grass. By eye the ramp is a dark base with about 3 speckle tones and a pink accent, so roughly 4 usable shading steps against 5-6 in the references. The speckles are sparse, uniform and evenly scattered, so there are no clumps, no per-stone shading and no tufts. The pink crack marks look like loose strokes rather than integrated structure. There are no outlines, so the sticker look is not a concern. The texture is real but noisy and repetitive, and it has less structure than the reference paving or the grass tufts. A careful artist would likely see it as a thinner, more generic noise fill than the references. When in doubt, fail.
